PAIN 1 - the action button cannot be tapped. The lane builds its bless action with url "answer:<topic>", which is not a URL scheme, so the phone refuses it. WITNESS: the owner, 2026-07-25, tapping a real card: 'Expected URL scheme http or https but was answer.' The design document had listed this exact leg as never verified (§19 item 3), and it shipped anyway.

PAIN 2 - the card carries no brief worth reading. It publishes the offer's first 400 characters as a bare message: no title distinguishing a gate from an ordinary question, no priority, no way to see the evidence behind the ask. WITNESS: engine/phone.ts announceOffer, and the message the owner actually received today, which said nothing about what was being decided.

PAIN 3 - the rich brief specified in the design does not exist in v2. §11 names it as tier 1 of the adjudication ladder and §18 records it as built and verified end to end on 2026-07-21 - Workers KV, key in the URL fragment, read-after-write before notifying. v2 has none of it: §19 item 2 records the adapter code as never written, and the §18 steps as manual curl. WITNESS: the design document's own open-items list, and v1, which HAS the equivalent (adr-handoff-html: one browsable page per bless moment, the same page travelling to the phone as the ask's link).

PAIN 4 - nothing says whether a publish worked. PhoneLane is constructed without a call log in the board, so a failed publish is swallowed entirely; a broken transport looks exactly like a quiet one. WITNESS: this session - the lane was silently doing nothing while appearing configured, and the only way to find out was to reproduce its HTTP call by hand.

PAIN 5 - the lane reads its configuration once, at board startup. Restoring or changing phone.json does nothing until the board is cycled, which no surface tells you. WITNESS: this session, where restoring the config left the lane inert until the board was restarted.

PAIN 6 - the agent has no rule for WHEN the phone matters. It paused the lane for an unattended run, which was fine, and then parked on a gate the owner was meant to bless without restoring it, which was not. WITNESS: i5d's release gate, which reached nobody until the owner asked why.
